one_liner: Builds and looks after websites and online shops for small businesses, usually freelance.
job_roles: WordPress Developer | Shopify Developer | Webflow Developer | Website Maintenance Freelancer | E-commerce Store Setup Specialist
self_emp_route: Freelance from the first client, then a small agency. This is the most common self-employment in Sector 1 and also the most exposed to no-code tools taking the low end.
ai_reason: Almost pure execution skill on digital output, which is the most exposed combination in the sector. What survives is the client relationship — knowing a local business well enough to run their store. Building the pages themselves is already largely automated. Raised clarity 20->25. The durable part of this work is understanding what a local business actually needs versus what they asked for — that is 'for whom' clarity. Page-building itself is fully exposed.
path_to_entry: self_study: Learn WordPress or Shopify — free, online, no gatekeeper -> portfolio: Build 3-5 real sites, even unpaid, for local businesses -> first_clients: Freelance platforms or local word of mouth
review_reason: SELF-EMPLOYMENT CEILING OWED. Employed mid-career is 4.5 lakh and people in this profession routinely go independent, but no reliable Indian figure was found for what they earn once they do. Until it exists the record understates the profession, which is exactly the defect this field was added to fix. The route is recorded; the number is not.
nuances: [demand_signal] Demand is declining. Wix, Shopify and no-code builders have absorbed most of the simple brochure-and-catalogue work that defined this job, and generative tools are taking the rest of the low end. What survives is integration, performance and commerce operations for businesses that have outgrown a template. Still listed - Indian small business is enormous and the work has not vanished - but the direction is down.

one_liner: Builds video games and 3D interactive worlds — the code, the rules and the environments.

self_emp_route: Indie studio or contract development for larger studios.
ai_reason: Asset production and boilerplate gameplay code are exposed. Judging what is actually fun, and why a level feels wrong, is clarity that does not transfer to a model.
role_spread: [AR Developer, VR Developer, Simulation Developer] higher: spatial, logical, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> training: Game development diploma, or self-taught Unity/Unreal -> portfolio: 2-3 finished playable games or XR demos. Studios hire on this, not marks.
nuances: [job_roles] AR and VR development is merged in here rather than standing alone. The engines are the same - Unity and Unreal - the studios are largely the same, and India's standalone XR market is small. Confirmed as a merge rather than a separate profession. || [job_roles] Game Designer and Level Designer were removed from this profession and moved to Sector 8, where Game Designer is now a profession in its own right. This record covers the people who BUILD the game; the people who decide what the game IS sit in Design & Creative Arts. A student searching for game work should be shown both.

one_liner: Teaches computers to recognise patterns, predict things and answer in language.

Treat the ceiling as cycle-dependent rather than structural. || [degree_dependency] Tagged undergrad because that is what the hiring market overwhelmingly screens on, not because the knowledge is unreachable otherwise. This is the profession in Sector 1 where a demonstrated portfolio - published models, competition results, real deployed systems - most often overrides the absence of a matching degree. The tag is the destination and the usual door; it is not the only door. || [economics] The widest band in the taxonomy, and the width is real rather than an artefact. The same job title covers someone fine-tuning an existing model against a vendor API and someone training models at scale in a research-adjacent team, and Indian pay for the second is set by a small global market while pay for the first is set by ordinary IT services rates.

role_spread: [Penetration Tester] higher: openness, reasoning, confidence / lower: agreeableness, dogmatism

A computer science degree helps and is the common path; it is not the gate. || [job_roles] Penetration Tester and Red Team Analyst are offensive-security roles, and the skills are the same ones an attacker uses. What separates the profession from the crime is authorisation - a signed scope agreement before any testing - and that distinction belongs in front of a school-age student at the point the role is shown, not after.

AICTE norms set NO maximum age for diploma-to-B.Tech lateral entry, so the three-year JEE window constrains one route and not the profession. What varies is the state: some state LEET rules and some institutions apply an 18 to 26 band, and the diploma aggregate requirement runs 45 to 50 percent. A student should check their own state's LEET, but no state closes the door outright.

one_liner: Plans how to extract coal, ore and minerals from the earth safely.
job_roles: Mine Planning Engineer | Mine Safety Officer | Blasting Engineer | Mineral Processing Engineer | Ventilation Engineer
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | JEE Advanced | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
ai_reason: Underground work cannot be done remotely, and statutory safety duties sit with a named person. Planning software is exposed; being the accountable officer below ground is not.
role_spread: [Mine Safety Officer] higher: emotional_intelligence, verbal, dogmatism / lower: spatial
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory, plus one of Chemistry/Biology/Vocational -> entrance_exam: JEE Main Paper 1, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Mining Engineering (4 years) -> specialisation: Internships and site or plant exposure decide who gets hired

nuances: [licensing_body] The degree gets you into the profession; the DGMS certificate gates the top of it. Under the Mines Act 1952 with the Coal Mines Regulations 2017 and the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961, the posts of Manager, Overman, Surveyor and Sirdar are STATUTORY - they can only be held by someone carrying a DGMS Certificate of Competency, and the holder carries personal legal liability for safety. First Class and Second Class Manager certificates require the degree or diploma PLUS documented underground or opencast experience, and are held for life subject to medical fitness. A mining engineer can work without one; they cannot run a mine.

one_liner: Runs and maintains the engines and machinery of ships at sea.
job_roles: Marine Engineer Officer | Engine Room Watchkeeper | Shipyard Engineer | Port & Dock Engineer | Marine Surveyor
ai_reason: Among the least exposed careers in the dataset. The work is physical, at sea, on machinery, and a licensed officer must hold the watch. Remote and autonomous shipping is decades from replacing this.
role_spread: [Marine Surveyor, Shipyard Engineer, Port & Dock Engineer] higher: verbal, conscientiousness / lower: bodily, neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry and Maths, usually with 60% and English at 50% -> entrance_exam: IMU CET or a DG Shipping approved institute entrance -> degree: B.Tech Marine Engineering at a DG Shipping approved institute (4 years) -> sea_time: Mandatory sea service on board ship -> licence: Certificate of Competency from the Directorate General of Shipping
nuances: [path_to_entry] Only DG Shipping approved institutes lead to a Certificate of Competency. A degree from a non-approved college does not qualify you to sail. College choice is itself a gate here, unlike most engineering. || [path_to_entry] The sea time is part of the qualification, not something that follows it. one_liner: Starts and runs a business — and carries the risk of it.
job_roles: Founder | Small Business Owner | Franchise Owner | D2C Brand Owner | Self-Employed Trader / Distributor | Co-Founder (operations)
industrial_sectors: MEPSC | RASCI | FICSI | AMHSSC | THSC | IT-ITES | LSC
self_emp_route: This profession IS self-employment; there is no employed version of it. The ceiling is genuinely unbounded upward and the floor is zero, which is why no ceiling figure is claimed.
ai_reason: Not meaningfully exposed as a whole, because the work is deciding what to do with incomplete information and living with the consequence. Individual tasks inside a small business are heavily automatable, which mostly makes one person able to run more.
path_to_entry: any_stage: No qualification exists and none is required — this is the only profession in the taxonomy you cannot be admitted to -> capability: Usually a trade, craft, technical or sales skill first; the business is built on top of something you can already do -> capital: Own savings, family capital, or a government scheme — MUDRA, PMEGP, Stand-Up India -> operation: Registration, GST, and the discipline of running it
review_reason: The economics are unlike anything else in the dataset: outcomes are extremely dispersed, survivorship bias is severe in every available source, and a range is close to meaningless. Decide whether to show numbers at all for this record, or present it with the range suppressed and the risk stated instead. Also decide whether it should surface for school-age users at all, or only for college and working-age ones.
nuances: [profession] This record strains the profession test and is included deliberately. Interest alignment is clear and the sector is named for it, but the SKILL SET is not separate — running a business is sales, operations and finance combined. It earns its place as the destination those skills combine into, and because leaving it out would make the sector's own name false. || [economics] The only record in the taxonomy whose early_earnings band starts at zero, and that is not a formatting artefact. A founder can earn nothing for years. Every other profession here pays from the first month. || [economics] economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Outcomes are extremely dispersed and survivorship bias is severe in every available source. Most new businesses do not reach a stable income at all. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it. This record was the FIRST to raise the problem, in Sector 5, and it took five more sectors independently asking for the same exception before the schema was changed.

one_liner: Drives goods and people for a living under a commercial licence - trucks, buses, ambulances.
job_roles: Heavy Vehicle Driver | Truck Driver | Bus Driver | State Transport Driver | Delivery Van Driver | Ambulance Driver | School Bus Driver | Tanker & Hazardous Goods Driver | Owner-Driver | Driving Instructor
self_emp_route: Owning a truck, van or bus and running it - the standard route above a driver's wage in Indian road transport. It is a leveraged small business: the EMI, fuel, maintenance and idle days all sit with the owner, and it can go badly wrong.
ai_reason: Very low exposure today and the largest long-horizon question of any base-layer profession in this dataset. Driving is physical control of a vehicle in unstructured traffic and nothing in the generative-AI wave touches it. AUTONOMOUS DRIVING IS THE REAL QUESTION and it is deliberately not scored as exposure here: Indian road conditions, mixed traffic and liability law make it far more distant than in the countries where the technology is being developed, and there is no sourced Indian timeline. A student entering this trade at 20 should know the question exists without being told a date nobody can source.
role_spread: [State Transport Driver, School Bus Driver] higher: conscientiousness, agreeableness, attention_span / lower: openness || [Tanker & Hazardous Goods Driver] higher: conscientiousness, logical, neuroticism / lower: extraversion || [Owner-Driver, Driving Instructor] higher: confidence, logical, verbal / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Most states require class 8 pass for a transport licence; a few require class 10. -> licence: A commercial or transport vehicle licence under the Motor Vehicles Act - a separate endorsement from a private licence, with a higher minimum age and a medical. -> training: A driver training institute, or learning under an experienced driver. Hazardous goods and passenger endorsements need specific training. -> work: Logistics company, a state transport corporation, a bus operator, a school, a hospital, or a fleet. Corporation posts are filled by state recruitment. -> independence: Own the vehicle. This is the route off a wage in Indian road transport, and it is capital and risk rather than promotion.
review_reason: Three gaps. No sourced wage figure for Indian commercial drivers at any level. No figure for what an owner-driver actually clears after EMI, fuel, maintenance and idle days - which is the named route up and the one most likely to be oversold to someone. And a presentation decision this record cannot make: it should be DESCRIBED but arguably never SUGGESTED to a school student, which is the third record to need that distinction after Waste Management & Sanitation Worker and Religious & Ritual Professional.
nuances: [job_roles] APP-BASED RIDE-HAILING AND FOOD DELIVERY ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this record, and the exclusion is the most important thing on it. Those are platform gig work: no employer, no ladder, no notice period, earnings claims that are routinely inflated in recruitment marketing, and a vehicle EMI that sits with the driver rather than the platform. This record covers LICENSED COMMERCIAL DRIVING - a transport endorsement, an employer, and in the case of a state transport corporation a permanent post with a pension. They are not the same occupation and presenting them as one is how the whole trade comes to look like gig work. || [economics] The employed figure is a driver's wage. Two things sit outside it and both matter more: a state transport corporation post is permanent government employment on a pay scale, and long-haul and hazardous goods driving pays materially above the base-layer trades because India has a documented shortage of licensed heavy vehicle drivers. Neither is sourced here. || [demand_signal] High and structurally so - road freight moves the overwhelming majority of Indian goods and the shortage of licensed heavy vehicle drivers is well documented in the logistics industry. This is demand for a licensed skill, not for gig labour.

one_liner: Checks that a company's accounts are true, and works out what it owes.

industrial_sectors: BFSI | MEPSC | IT-ITES | RASCI | CGSC | EXT-GOVT
licensing_body: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
self_emp_route: Own practice after ICAI membership — audit, tax and advisory for small and mid-sized businesses. The most common destination in the profession, and it needs a certificate of practice, not capital.
ai_reason: Reconciliation, ledger scrutiny and return preparation are heavily exposed and already automating. What protects the profession is that the SIGNATURE carries statutory liability — an audit opinion is a person taking legal responsibility, which software cannot do.
role_spread: [Forensic Auditor, Internal Auditor] higher: reasoning, openness, dogmatism / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_12: ANY stream — commerce, science or arts all qualify for CA Foundation -> foundation: CA Foundation; graduates with the required percentage skip it and enter Intermediate directly -> intermediate: CA Intermediate, two groups -> articleship: THREE YEARS of articleship training under a practising CA — this is the qualification, not an internship -> final: CA Final plus the mandatory AICITSS course, then ICAI membership
review_reason: COST & MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT (ICMAI) is not listed as a separate profession. ICMAI is a statutory body under the Cost and Works Accountants Act 1959 with its own three-stage route, so it arguably deserves its own record; it is currently absent rather than merged. Verify the ICMAI route and decide.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] CA is open after class 12 from ANY stream, including arts. It is one of the very few high-earning Indian professions with no subject gate at all, and it does not require a degree — a fact frequently missed by students who assume commerce is compulsory. || [years_to_qualify] The three-year articleship is part of the qualification, not experience after it. That is why the realistic time is about five years and why the pass rate, not the admission, is the real filter.

one_liner: Keeps the books straight — entries, invoices, GST and payroll.

industrial_sectors: BFSI | MEPSC | RASCI | IT-ITES | FICSI | LSC
self_emp_route: Independent bookkeeping and GST filing practice serving several small businesses — very low capital, built on local relationships.
ai_reason: THE MOST EXPOSED PROFESSION IN THIS SECTOR. Data entry, reconciliation, invoice matching and return preparation are exactly what automation does best, and accounting software is absorbing them fast. The client relationship at the small-business end is what remains.
path_to_entry: class_12: Commerce is usual but not required -> certificate: Tally, Zoho Books or a similar accounting package — this is what employers screen on -> degree: A B.Com helps and is common, but is not the gate -> employment: Every business of any size, plus accounting and outsourcing firms
review_reason: SITS EXACTLY ON THE FILTER BOUNDARY, and survives by rounding. Mid-career midpoint is 6.0 and AI exposure is high at 75 — the compensation rule cuts a profession below 6.0 with high exposure, so a tenth of a lakh either way decides whether this ships. It is also the most AI-exposed record in Sector 6 and one of the largest entry-level employers of commerce graduates in India. Two decisions: whether the band is right, and whether a profession this exposed should be recommended as a destination or only as a route into Chartered Accountancy.
nuances: [professional_sector] The base layer of finance, listed beside Chartered Accountant at the apex on the same principle as Mason beside Civil Engineer. It is also the most realistic formal-sector entry point in finance for a student without the time or money for a five-year professional qualification.

one_liner: Prices risk, and decides what a claim is really worth.

role_spread: [Medical Coder, Medical Biller, Claims Analyst (health)] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: extraversion, reasoning

Classifying documents against a published rulebook to get a payer to pay is claims work; the documents being medical is the industry, which is why HSSC is a tag here rather than the sector. || [ai_exposure] The coding and billing roles are far more exposed than the profession's overall score, and they are also its largest employers by headcount. A student entering through that door should be told they are at the exposed end.

one_liner: Manages other people's money and advises them where to put it.

self_emp_route: Independent financial advisory practice, which needs SEBI registration and NISM certification rather than capital. Income moves with assets under advice.

one_liner: Uses mathematics to price risk decades into the future.
job_roles: Actuarial Analyst | Pricing Actuary | Reserving Actuary | Valuation Actuary | Actuarial Consultant | Risk Modelling Analyst
self_emp_route: Independent actuarial consulting after qualification, typically to smaller insurers and pension schemes.
ai_reason: Heavily quantitative but built on foundational mathematics rather than retrievable knowledge, and the output is a professional judgment an insurer relies on. Model automation assists it rather than replacing it.
path_to_entry: class_12: Strong mathematics is effectively required even where it is not formally mandated -> entrance: ACET, the Institute of Actuaries of India entrance test -> exams: A long series of professional examinations taken while working — most candidates take many years -> employment: Life and general insurers, reinsurers, consulting firms, pension advisers
nuances: [years_to_qualify] Seven years is the realistic figure and it may be optimistic. The professional examinations have low pass rates and are taken alongside full-time work, so many candidates take a decade and a substantial number never complete them. Anyone considering this should treat the exam sequence, not the entrance test, as the real gate. || [licensing_body] The Actuaries Act 2006 does not merely regulate the title — its DEFINITION of an actuary includes being a fellow member of the Institute of Actuaries of India. You cannot be an actuary in Indian law without IAI fellowship, which makes this one of the hardest statutory gates in the taxonomy.

one_liner: Studies how money, work and policy move through a whole economy.

entrance_exams: CUET (BA/B.Sc Economics) | DSE / ISI / JNU entrance (MA) | RBI Grade B (DEPR) | Indian Economic Service (UPSC)
self_emp_route: Independent research and policy consulting to think tanks, industry bodies and international agencies.
ai_reason: Data work and literature summarising are exposed. Framing an economic question and defending a policy judgment in public are not — the clarity and foundational-knowledge shares carry it.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream; mathematics is a strong advantage and required by some programmes -> degree: BA or B.Sc Economics -> post_graduate: MA or M.Sc Economics is the real entry qualification; DSE, ISI, JNU and IGIDR are the recognised routes -> employment: RBI and government, banks and rating agencies, think tanks, international organisations
nuances: [professional_sector] Routed here from Sector 3 Science & Research. Economics is empirical, but its object of concern is money and value, and it has its own professional sector. Research method alone does not decide the sector when a sector exists for the subject itself. || [mid_stream_entry] Corrected from restart_undergrad. An MA or M.Sc Economics does not require a bachelor's in economics — engineering, mathematics, statistics and commerce graduates enter routinely, and several of the strongest Indian programmes prefer a mathematical background over an economics one. The subject gate is mathematics ability, not a prior economics degree.

one_liner: Argues and advises on what the law allows, requires and forbids.

entrance_exams: CLAT | AILET | LSAT India | AIBE (after enrolment) | CUET (LLB) | SLAT
self_emp_route: Independent practice is the traditional shape of the profession — chambers first, then your own. Needs enrolment and a Certificate of Practice rather than capital.

one_liner: Makes sure a company follows the law it is required to follow.
job_roles: Company Secretary | Compliance Officer | Secretarial Auditor | Corporate Governance Analyst | Legal & Secretarial Executive | Listing Compliance Officer

Apply the sector test: delete company law and the role disappears entirely. Its object of concern is whether the organisation obeys the law, which is governance, not money. It is a separate profession from Corporate Lawyer — different statutory qualification, different daily work.

one_liner: Enforces the law, investigates crime and keeps public order.

nuances: [professional_sector] Police sits here under the cross-cutting rule: a uniformed identity whose work exists because the state exists belongs to Sector 7. A forensic scientist employed by the same police department does NOT — they keep their home sector with a government tag. || [ai_exposure] legal_accountability is true with no licensing_body. Powers of arrest, search and seizure, and personal liability for their misuse, come from the Police Acts and the CrPC rather than from any licensing council. || [verification] Entry is controlled by examination — UPSC Civil Services for the IPS, SSC CPO and state police recruitment boards for Sub-Inspector and Constable. one_liner: Sits as a judge in the district courts and decides cases.
job_roles: Civil Judge (Junior Division) | Judicial Magistrate | Additional District Judge | Judicial Officer | Court Registrar
entrance_exams: State Judicial Services Examination (Civil Judge) | Higher Judicial Services Examination
ai_reason: The highest combined foundational-knowledge and clarity share in the taxonomy. Judging is applying law to disputed facts and being personally accountable for the outcome — the most structurally protected work in the dataset.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: LLB — five-year integrated after class 12, or three-year after any degree -> enrolment: Bar Council enrolment; some states require years of practice for the higher entry -> exam: State Judicial Services Examination, conducted by the High Court or State PSC -> service: Appointment as a Civil Judge, then progression through the district judiciary
nuances: [profession] A separate profession from Lawyer, not a senior version of one. Entry is by a distinct state examination taken after the LLB, and many judicial officers are appointed as fresh law graduates without practising as advocates at all. || [licensing_body] Null, and it was WRONG before - this record named the Bar Council of India. A judge does not practise under a BCI licence. An advocate who takes full-time service is moved to the non-practising list and surrenders their enrolment certificate, and the BCI has no power to strike off a judge. BCI enrolment is a PREREQUISITE for eligibility, which is a path_to_entry step, not a licence to practise. Control over the subordinate judiciary vests in the High Court under Article 235 of the Constitution, which is appointment and discipline rather than licensing. || [ai_exposure] legal_accountability is true with no licensing_body, on the same statutory-office footing as Civil Services Officer, Police Officer and Armed Forces Officer in this sector. A judge is personally answerable for judicial orders by virtue of holding office, and the orders are appealable. There is no unlicensed version of this work to police: you cannot practise as a judge without being appointed one, which is why the licensing frame does not apply here at all. || [degree_dependency] 'undergrad' understates the qualification slightly and is the accurate value for how this profession is ENTERED. An LLB is a professional degree, but this record is not a licensed practice - it is an office reached by appointment after a state examination, exactly like the three other uniformed and administrative services in this sector, all of which are 'undergrad'. The LLB requirement is carried in path_to_entry where it belongs.

one_liner: Researches and designs the rules and programmes governments run on.
job_roles: Policy Analyst | Policy Researcher | Legislative Assistant | Programme Evaluation Analyst | Government Affairs Analyst | Regulatory Affairs Analyst (policy)
entrance_exams: CUET PG | Institute entrances (NLS, TISS, Ashoka, IIM public policy)
self_emp_route: Independent policy consulting to foundations, industry bodies and international organisations.
ai_reason: Literature review and drafting are exposed. Deciding which problem a policy should solve, and for whom, is the clarity that carries this profession.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's; economics, law, political science and engineering all feed in -> post_graduate: MPP or MA in public policy is the usual entry qualification -> employment: Think tanks, LAMP fellowships, government advisory units, foundations, corporate government-affairs teams
nuances: [professional_sector] Distinct from Research Psychologist and other Sector 3 researchers, which study the world to know it. Policy work exists to CHANGE what the state does — without a state there is no policy profession, which is the Sector 7 test.

one_liner: Does the research, drafting and paperwork a legal team runs on.
job_roles: Paralegal | Legal Assistant | Contract Management Executive | Legal Operations Executive | Court Clerk | Documentation Executive (legal) | Compliance Assistant
self_emp_route: Freelance contract drafting and documentation support for small firms and startups.
ai_reason: THE MOST EXPOSED PROFESSION IN THIS SECTOR by a wide margin. Document review, contract abstraction and legal research are exactly what language models do well, and legal process outsourcing is built on that work. There is no licence and no personal liability to protect it.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> certificate: Paralegal or legal-support diploma; a BA LLB is not required -> degree: Any bachelor's helps; law graduates awaiting enrolment often start here -> employment: Law firms, in-house legal teams, legal process outsourcing firms, courts
review_reason: Highest AI exposure in Sector 7 and no licence to protect it, in a profession whose Indian employment sits largely in legal process outsourcing for foreign firms — the segment most directly substitutable. It is also a genuine entry route for law graduates awaiting enrolment. Decide how strongly to frame the exposure.
nuances: [professional_sector] The base layer of the legal pyramid, listed beside Lawyer at its apex. It is also the only unlicensed profession in this sector, which is exactly why it is the most AI-exposed one — the licence and the liability are what protect the others.

one_liner: Runs towards fires, collapses and accidents to get people out.
job_roles: Firefighter | Fire Operator | Rescue Operator | Municipal Fire Officer | Emergency Response Operator | Fire Station Officer
entrance_exams: State fire service recruitment examinations | Municipal corporation recruitment
ai_reason: Among the least exposed work in the entire taxonomy. Entering a burning building and cutting someone out of a car is physical, unstructured and irreducibly human.
path_to_entry: class_12: Class 12 in any stream; some state cadres take class 10 -> physical: Height, chest, endurance and running standards - a genuine and strict gate -> exam: State fire service or municipal corporation recruitment; some states recruit through the police board -> training: State fire service training academy -> employment: State fire services, municipal corporations, airports, refineries, large industrial plants
nuances: [professional_sector] Routed here from Sector 2, where Fire & Safety Engineer sits. The split is that the engineer DESIGNS systems so a fire never starts, which is engineering; the firefighter is a uniformed public servant who responds when it does, which is the Sector 7 cross-cutting rule.

one_liner: Writes and files patents, and argues for them at the patent office.
job_roles: Patent Agent | Patent Analyst | Patent Drafting Specialist | Prior Art Search Analyst | IP Paralegal | Patent Prosecution Associate
licensing_body: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (Register of Patent Agents)
self_emp_route: Independent patent practice once registered - drafting and prosecution for startups and research institutions.
ai_reason: Prior-art searching and first-draft claim writing are directly exposed. A registered agent signs filings and answers for them, and the claim-drafting judgment that decides how broad a patent is remains the craft.
path_to_entry: class_12: Science stream in practice, because the degree below requires it -> degree: A degree in science, pharmacy, engineering or technology from a university established under Indian law — a hard requirement under Section 126 of the Patents Act 1970. A law degree alone does NOT qualify you. -> exam: The Patent Agent Examination conducted by the Indian Patent Office -> registration: Registration on the Register of Patent Agents -> employment: IP law firms, corporate IP teams, research organisations, IP analytics firms
nuances: [professional_sector] Routed here from Sector 3. The subject matter is science but the work is law - delete the Patents Act and the profession disappears, which is the Sector 7 test. Sector 3 keeps the research the patent describes. || [path_to_entry] The requirement runs opposite to most legal careers: a SCIENCE OR ENGINEERING degree is mandatory and a law degree alone does not qualify you to sit the examination. One of the few routes where a B.Tech or B.Sc graduate has an advantage over an LLB holder. || [licensing_body] Section 126 of the Patents Act 1970 sets four conditions: Indian citizenship, age at least 21, a science, pharmacy, engineering or technology degree from an Indian university, and passing the qualifying examination — or ten years of service as a patent examiner. Section 125 requires the Controller General to maintain the Register of Patent Agents, and until your name is on it you cannot lawfully practise. That makes this Tier A in the strict sense: practising unregistered is unlawful, not merely unrecognised.

one_liner: Makes information look right and read clearly - logos, packaging, posters, brand systems.
job_roles: Graphic Designer | Brand Identity Designer | Packaging Designer | Layout & Publication Designer | Motion Graphics Designer | Signage & Wayfinding Designer | Social Media Creative Designer | Typographer
self_emp_route: Freelance and small-studio work built off the same portfolio used to get hired; a one-person studio serving local businesses is the commonest form.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. Generative image tools now produce competent layouts, social creatives and packaging mockups from a prompt, and that is exactly the entry-level work a junior is hired to do. Social Media Creative Designer and Layout & Publication Designer face this first. Brand Identity Designer is the protected end - the work there is deciding what a company should look like and defending the call to people who disagree, which is clarity, not output.
role_spread: [Motion Graphics Designer] higher: spatial, logical / lower: verbal || [Brand Identity Designer] higher: verbal, openness, confidence / lower: attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. No subject is required. -> training: A 1-2 year diploma in graphic or communication design, or a B.Des. Neither is legally required. -> portfolio: Build a portfolio of 10-15 real pieces. This, not the certificate, is what gets read at hiring. -> work: Junior designer at a studio, agency or in-house brand team; or freelance from the portfolio directly.
nuances: [degree_dependency] There is no qualification here at all. The portfolio IS the credential, and a self-taught designer with good work competes directly with a B.Des graduate. That cuts both ways: entry is genuinely open, and nothing protects the practitioner from being undercut. || [ai_exposure] The bottom rung is shrinking, not the profession. Studios still need someone to decide what is right and take responsibility for it - what they need fewer of is people to produce the twentieth variation of a banner.

one_liner: Designs how an app or website works and feels, so people can use it without being taught.
job_roles: UX Designer | UI Designer | Interaction Designer | UX Researcher | Design Systems Designer | Information Architect | Usability Analyst | Service Designer | Product Designer (Digital)
self_emp_route: Freelance product design for startups, or a small independent studio. Common after 4-6 years, once a case-study portfolio can win work on its own.
ai_reason: Screens generate easily; understanding does not. UI Designer is the exposed role - tools already produce clean, conventional layouts from a description. UX Researcher and Service Designer are the protected end, for the same reason an IT Business Analyst is: the work is establishing what a room of people who disagree actually need, and a model cannot know whose problem it is.
role_spread: [UX Researcher, Usability Analyst] higher: verbal, emotional_intelligence, reasoning / lower: spatial || [Design Systems Designer] higher: conscientiousness, logical, attention_span / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Des, or any bachelor's degree followed by a UX course. Psychology, English and engineering graduates all enter this way. -> portfolio: Three or four case studies showing a problem, the research, the decisions and the outcome - not just screens. -> work: Junior UX or UI designer on a product team.
nuances: [industrial_sectors] Routed here from Sector 1. The tools are digital and the employer is usually a software company, but the object of concern is the person using the product - swap the software out for a hospital form or an ATM and the work survives unchanged. || [entry_competition] Null on purpose. This is one of the few well-paid Indian professions with no gate of any kind - no exam, no licence, no required degree subject. A commerce or arts graduate can enter it directly, which is rare in this dataset.

one_liner: Makes drawings and digital models move - for film, series, games and advertising.
job_roles: 2D Animator | 3D Animator | Character Rigger | VFX Compositor | Modelling & Texturing Artist | Lighting & Rendering Artist | Storyboard Artist | Matchmove Artist | Roto & Paint Artist | Motion Capture Artist
self_emp_route: Freelance shots and sequences for studios, which is how a large part of the industry already works; established artists take contract work directly from overseas clients.
ai_reason: Generative video and automated rotoscoping attack this profession from the bottom, which is the worst place to be attacked. Roto & Paint Artist and Matchmove Artist are the exposed roles, and they are precisely the rungs India's outsourced VFX industry hires at volume. Character Rigger, Lighting & Rendering Artist and Storyboard Artist are more protected - rigging is engineering a puppet that must behave under any motion, and storyboarding is narrative judgment.
role_spread: [Roto & Paint Artist, Matchmove Artist] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: openness, verbal || [Storyboard Artist] higher: verbal, openness, reasoning / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Sc or BA in Animation, B.Des, or any degree plus a 1-2 year animation and VFX diploma. -> showreel: A 60-90 second showreel in ONE discipline. Studios hire for a seat on a pipeline, not for general ability. -> work: Junior artist at a VFX or animation studio, usually starting on roto, paint or matchmove.
nuances: [demand_signal] Pathway is 'any' because India is a global outsourcing centre for VFX and animation post-production, so a large share of the work is done here for foreign studios. That is also the vulnerability: the same economics that brought the work can move it. || [ai_exposure] The bottom rung is shrinking, not the career. A rigger or a lighting artist with five years of pipeline experience is not replaceable by a prompt - but the roto seat that used to be how those five years began is.

one_liner: Draws what does not exist yet - characters, worlds, book art, comics and editorial images.
job_roles: Illustrator | Concept Artist | Comic & Graphic Novel Artist | Children's Book Illustrator | Editorial Illustrator | Character Designer | Matte Painter | Scientific & Medical Illustrator | Caricaturist
self_emp_route: Commissions taken directly from publishers, studios and agencies, plus print and licensing income from your own work. Most illustrators are self-employed from day one.
ai_reason: The single most exposed profession in this dataset, and it would be dishonest to soften it. Text-to-image models were trained on exactly this output and produce it at near-zero marginal cost. Editorial Illustrator, Matte Painter and general Illustrator commissions are already contracting. What holds: Scientific & Medical Illustrator, where a named human is accountable for the accuracy of a diagram a surgeon will rely on, and Comic & Graphic Novel Artist, where the reader is buying an authored voice across hundreds of pages, not an image.
role_spread: [Scientific & Medical Illustrator] higher: conscientiousness, naturalistic, attention_span / lower: openness || [Comic & Graphic Novel Artist] higher: verbal, long_term_memory / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> practice: Draw for two to three years and build a body of work. A BFA or design diploma helps and is not required. -> portfolio: A public portfolio and a visible style. Commissions come from being findable. -> work: Commissions from publishers, studios and agencies; or a staff concept artist seat at a game or animation studio.
nuances: [ai_exposure] Listed at high exposure and kept, because the rule for dropping a profession is technological obsolescence of the NEED, not of the current method. People still want drawn worlds, comics and picture books. What has collapsed is the price of a single competent image. || [economics] The employed figures describe a staff concept artist at a game or animation studio. A freelance illustrator's income is lumpy and commission-driven, and the range understates both its floor and its ceiling.

one_liner: Decides what a game is and how it plays - rules, levels, difficulty, economy and story.
job_roles: Game Designer | Level Designer | Narrative Designer | Systems & Economy Designer | Environment Artist | Character Artist (Games) | UI Designer (Games) | Technical Designer | Playtest & Balance Analyst
self_emp_route: Independent release on Steam, itch.io or the app stores, usually as a two-to-five person team. Realistic only after several years of shipped experience.
ai_reason: A clarity-heavy profession, which is what protects it. Environment Artist and Character Artist (Games) are exposed - they are asset production and generative tools reach them directly. Game Designer, Level Designer and Systems & Economy Designer are protected: the work is deciding what would be fun for a specific audience and then being proved wrong in playtesting, which is a judgment loop rather than an output task.
role_spread: [Narrative Designer] higher: verbal, openness, long_term_memory / lower: logical || [Systems & Economy Designer, Playtest & Balance Analyst] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree. Game design programmes exist but studios hire on shipped work. -> portfolio: Two or three finished small games, or levels and mods built in Unity or Unreal. Finished beats ambitious. -> work: Junior designer or QA-to-design at a studio; India's studios cluster in Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad and Mumbai.
nuances: [industrial_sectors] Distinct from Sector 1's Game & Interactive Media Developer, and the substitution test is what separates them. Remove the game from the developer and a software engineer remains; remove it from the designer and nothing does. One writes the engine, the other decides what the engine should make you feel. || [demand_signal] Moderate, not high. India has a very large games MARKET and a much smaller game DEVELOPMENT industry - most Indian studios do art and engineering services for foreign titles rather than original design. Reading market size as the number of design jobs is the error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against.

one_liner: Plans the inside of homes, shops and offices - layout, light, materials and furniture.
job_roles: Interior Designer | Space Planner | Retail & Store Design Specialist | Fixture & Joinery Designer | Lighting Designer | Exhibition & Stall Designer | Interior Project Coordinator | Modular Kitchen Specialist | Interior Stylist
self_emp_route: Independent practice, usually as a design-and-build studio taking a margin on execution as well as a design fee. This is the normal shape of the profession in India, not an exception.
ai_reason: Layout options and renders generate easily, and Interior Stylist and Space Planner feel that first. What does not automate is the middle of the job: standing on a site where the wall is 40mm out, the client has changed their mind and the carpenter has cut the wrong sheet. Interior Project Coordinator and Fixture & Joinery Designer are protected by that reality.
role_spread: [Lighting Designer] higher: spatial, logical, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Interior Project Coordinator] higher: conscientiousness, extraversion / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Des or B.Sc in Interior Design (4 years), or a 1-2 year diploma. Neither is legally required to practise. -> site_experience: Two to three years with a firm, learning execution - materials, vendors, costing and site supervision. -> work: Designer at a studio or design-and-build firm, or independent practice.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and this is the sector's most consequential settled fact. The Architects Act 1972 protects the TITLE 'architect' - it does not protect the ACTIVITY of designing interiors. Anyone in India may design and execute an interior with no registration and no degree. The Institute of Indian Interior Designers is a voluntary professional association, not a statutory regulator. || [economics] The employed range describes a designer on a firm's payroll. Independent practice earns on execution margin rather than fee, and that is where the real income in this profession sits - which is exactly what mid_career_lpa excludes by design.

one_liner: Designs physical products - appliances, tools, vehicles, medical devices, furniture.
job_roles: Industrial Designer | Product Designer (Hardware) | Furniture Designer | Transportation Designer | Toy Designer | CMF Designer | Packaging Structure Designer | Design Researcher | Model Maker & Prototyper
self_emp_route: Independent design consultancy serving manufacturers, normally after 5-8 years in-house - the work comes from a network, not a portfolio site.
ai_reason: The least exposed design profession here, because the output has to survive manufacture. A model can generate a beautiful kettle; it cannot know the tooling budget, the draft angles, the certification regime or what the factory can actually make. CMF Designer and Packaging Structure Designer are the more exposed roles; Design Researcher and Model Maker & Prototyper are the least.

The rest of the profession is protected by cloth: fit, drape, fabric behaviour and how a garment moves on a body are physical problems learned by making, and a design that cannot be sewn at a price is not a design. The public image of the profession comes from the very small number who run a successful label, and that income is entrepreneurship, excluded from mid_career_lpa by design. || [entry_competition] NIFT at 3.7 applicants per seat is the MOST OPEN national design gate in the registry - 17 times easier to enter than UCEED. The NIFT B.F.Tech degree route requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in class 12; the diploma and trade routes require nothing. one_liner: Cuts and sews clothing to measure or to a pattern - the base of the whole apparel industry.
job_roles: Tailor | Sewing Machine Operator | Boutique Tailor | Alteration Specialist | Hand & Machine Embroiderer | Cutting Master | Ethnic Wear Specialist | Bespoke Suit Tailor

ai_reason: Almost untouchable. Sewing a garment to fit a specific person is physical work in an unstructured environment, and every attempt to automate garment assembly has foundered on the fact that cloth is limp and will not hold its shape. Sewing Machine Operator is the only role with real exposure, and that is to automation of the factory line rather than to AI.
role_spread: [Sewing Machine Operator] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: verbal, extraversion, openness || [Bespoke Suit Tailor, Cutting Master] higher: spatial, bodily, long_term_memory / lower: neuroticism

Many enter after class 8 or 10. -> training: Apprenticeship with a working tailor, an ITI Sewing Technology trade, or an NSQF short course. -> work: Operator at a garment unit, or with a neighbourhood tailor. -> independence: Own shop with one to three machines, which is where the income actually changes.
review_reason: No sourced figure exists for what an independent tailor or boutique owner earns. Without it the record shows 3.0 LPA and reads as a dead end, when independence is the normal path in this trade and the reason people enter it. This is the same gap flagged on Mason in Sector 2 and needs the same fix: a sourced self_employment.ceiling_lpa.
nuances: [economics] These are EMPLOYED figures, largely piece-rate work in garment units, and they sit close to the legal minimum wage. They are not what a tailor with an established shop earns, and the record has no sourced figure for that - which is what the admin_review is for. || [demand_signal] High and stable, and worth stating plainly because the trade looks old-fashioned. Indian clothing is still overwhelmingly stitched to measure or altered after purchase, and both are jobs nobody has found a way to do remotely.

one_liner: Weaves cloth by hand on a loom - saris, stoles and yardage, mostly at home.
job_roles: Handloom Weaver | Jacquard Weaver | Dyer | Warper & Sizer | Design Card Maker | Loom Mechanic | Natural Dye Specialist | Handloom Cluster Coordinator
self_emp_route: Weaving on your own loom and selling direct - through a cooperative, a state emporium, a design label or online - instead of on piece rate for a master weaver. Direct sale is the single biggest determinant of a weaver's income.
ai_reason: The lowest AI exposure in this sector and among the lowest in the dataset. Handloom weaving is defined by being done by hand; the moment it is automated it becomes powerloom cloth, a different product in a different market. The threat to this profession has never been software - it is powerloom competition and the price of yarn.
role_spread: [Handloom Cluster Coordinator] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Loom Mechanic, Design Card Maker] higher: spatial, logical / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. The trade is usually learned at home from a parent, starting in the early teens. -> training: Family apprenticeship, or a Weavers' Service Centre or Indian Institute of Handloom Technology course. -> work: Weaving on piece rate for a master weaver or a cooperative society. -> independence: Own loom, selling through a cooperative, a state emporium or direct online sale.
review_reason: No sourced figure exists for what a weaver selling DIRECT earns - through a cooperative, an emporium or a design collaboration. That number is the whole difference between the census distribution and a viable livelihood, and without it the record shows only the piece-rate floor.

The range shown is that distribution converted to lakh per year. || [demand_signal] 26.7 lakh weavers and 8.5 lakh allied workers is a very large headcount, and reading it as opportunity would be the exact error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against. Demand for handloom CLOTH is steady; demand for a weaver's LABOUR is priced at subsistence. Both are true and a student needs to be told both. || [filter] Fails the compensation filter at 1.2 LPA, and rightly - but the profession is listed anyway. It is not disappearing, it is where 26.7 lakh people already are, and the application can reverse the filter for a student who is one of them.

one_liner: Makes objects by hand as a trade - pottery, woodwork, metalware, cane, embroidery.
job_roles: Potter | Wood Carver | Metal Craftsperson | Cane & Bamboo Artisan | Hand Embroiderer | Stone Carver | Block Printer | Terracotta Artisan | Toy & Doll Maker | Lacquerware Artisan
self_emp_route: Selling your own work directly - at exhibitions and melas, through a state emporium, or on an online marketplace - rather than producing on piece rate for an exporter. An artisan identity card unlocks the scheme and exhibition side of that.
ai_reason: As close to unexposed as this dataset contains. Every one of these roles is hand skill applied to a physical material in an unstructured setting, and part of the product's value is that a person made it. Where AI touches the trade at all it is on the selling side - listings, photographs and descriptions - not on the making.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Most craft skills are inherited within a family or a community. -> training: Apprenticeship under a working artisan, or a Guru-Shishya or design development scheme of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts). -> registration: Artisan identity card, which is what opens access to government schemes, exhibitions and credit. -> work: Producing on order for exporters and buyers, or selling direct at melas, emporia and online marketplaces.
review_reason: Two gaps, both money. There is no sourced income figure for handicraft artisans at all, and none for what an artisan selling direct earns versus one on piece rate for an exporter. Until both exist this is the least evidenced record in the sector, and it describes 6.4 million people.
nuances: [demand_signal] 6.4 million artisans is INDUSTRY SIZE, not profession size, and the distinction matters more here than almost anywhere. The headcount is enormous and shrinking in real terms as younger family members leave; demand for the output is real but concentrated in exports and tourism, both volatile. || [economics] Judgment, with no sources, and that is a genuine failure rather than a shrug. No usable earnings survey for Indian handicraft artisans was found. The figures shown are reasoned from the handloom census next door - a related trade with a similar structure - and should not be trusted until sourced. || [role_spread] Narrow despite ten very different materials. A potter and a cane worker look unalike but sit in almost the same psychometric place: hand skill, patience, spatial judgment, tolerance for repetition and an informal income. The material differs; the person the work suits does not.

one_liner: Designs and makes jewellery - from bench work at the anvil to CAD for a retail chain.

self_emp_route: Own karigar workshop taking order work from retailers and wholesalers - the dominant structure of Indian jewellery manufacture, which is a network of small independent units rather than factories.
ai_reason: The bench is safe; the drawing board is not. Goldsmith, Bench Jeweller, Diamond & Gemstone Setter and Polisher & Finisher are hand skills on precious material where a mistake is unrecoverable, and none of that is a text problem. CAD Jewellery Designer is the exposed role - generating ring variations on a theme is exactly what these tools do - and Gemmologist sits in between, since machine grading of stones is already deployed commercially.
role_spread: [Jewellery Designer, CAD Jewellery Designer] higher: spatial, openness, logical / lower: bodily || [Gemmologist] higher: attention_span, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: bodily

Hallmarking regulates the PRODUCT and the seller, not the craftsperson, and skill in this trade is certified by apprenticeship and reputation inside a karigar network rather than by any council. || [role_spread] This is a single profession containing two quite different people, kept as one because they share an object of concern and a workshop. A student should read the deviating roles before choosing: the bench route needs no degree and no English; the CAD route needs both.

one_liner: Comes up with the idea behind an ad and writes the words that carry it.

That rung is going, which means the profession may keep its senior jobs while losing the ladder that produced them. || [mid_stream_entry] One of the most open well-paid entries in the dataset. one_liner: Makes art as the work itself - painting, sculpture, printmaking, murals, installation.

self_emp_route: Selling through galleries, commissions, residencies and direct sale. Practically every practising fine artist is self-employed by definition - the question is what subsidises the practice, and for most it is teaching or design work.

Image generation devalues illustration, which sells the picture; it does not touch a sculpture, a print run or a commissioned mural. Portrait Artist is the most exposed role, and even there the market is largely for a painted object rather than a likeness.
role_spread: [Muralist & Public Artist] higher: extraversion, bodily, conscientiousness / lower: neuroticism || [Studio Assistant, Art Handler & Installer] higher: conscientiousness, bodily / lower: openness, confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: BFA (4 years) at a government art college or university department. Not legally required, but it is where a practice and a network usually start. -> practice: Build a body of work and exhibit - group shows, residencies, art fairs. -> work: Gallery representation and commissions, almost always alongside teaching, design work or studio assisting.

The record also has no figure for what gallery representation actually changes, which is the single most important economic fact in this profession.

India has a small collecting market and few public art budgets, so the number of people who live on art alone is genuinely small. The work exists and is done; it is rarely a whole income. || [economics] The range is wide and skewed because the distribution is: a small number of represented artists earn very well and most earn little from art itself. The figures assume a practice subsidised by teaching or design work, which is the normal case.

one_liner: Designs and makes shoes, bags and leather goods - form, fit, materials and the last.

The trade has its own Skill Council and its own national institute for the same reason. || [job_roles] Cobbler & Shoe Repair Specialist is deliberately inside this profession rather than left out as too small. one_liner: Finds out what happened, checks it, and tells the public - in print, on air or online.

entrance_exams: IIMC entrance | CUET UG | CUET PG | Symbiosis SET (Mass Communication)
self_emp_route: Freelance reporting, a subscriber-funded newsletter or an independent digital outlet. Increasingly common in India as staff newsrooms shrink, and it is where much of the serious reporting now happens.

Sub-Editor & Copy Editor and Business Journalist on routine numbers are the exposed roles. What no model can do is be in the room: Correspondent, Photojournalist and any reporting that depends on a source trusting a named person are protected, and Fact-Checker is protected by being the answer to the problem.

A BA or MA in journalism or mass communication is common and is not required - subject expertise in economics, law or science is often worth more. -> clips: Published work. one_liner: Builds everything you hear that is not music - dialogue, effects, atmosphere, the mix.

one_liner: The crew that makes a shoot physically happen - rigging, grip, power, sets, studio floor.

self_emp_route: Owning equipment and hiring it out with yourself attached - lights, grip gear or a camera package. This is the standard way crew income rises in Indian film and events, and it is capital, not promotion.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed, and for the plainest reason in the model: this is physical work in an unstructured space. Nothing generative rigs a light, lays a dolly track or loads a van. nuances: [economics] The base layer of the film and television industry, and the pay reflects that: it fails the compensation filter. one_liner: Performs music for a living - on stage, in a studio, at a temple, or at a wedding.

entrance_exams: Akashvani music audition (grading, not entry) | CUET UG (BA Music)
self_emp_route: Performance fees, session work, private teaching and recording, usually all at once. Practically every Indian musician is self-employed and assembles an income from three or four sources rather than one.
ai_reason: Low exposure and the reason is specific: what is bought here is a live human performing in a room, and generated audio does not substitute for that. Where exposure does bite is recorded and functional music - Session Musician work on advertising beds and library music is the role most at risk, because that market buys a sound rather than a performer. Classical Vocalist, Accompanist and Devotional & Temple Musician are essentially untouched.

Years, not months - classical training runs a decade. -> credential: Optional but useful: an Akashvani audition grade, which opens broadcast bookings. It licenses nothing. -> work: Performance, session work, accompaniment, recording and teaching - almost every working musician does several of these.
review_reason: There is no employed version of this profession at any scale in India, so mid_career_lpa - which is EMPLOYED-ONLY by design - describes almost nobody. No sourced figure exists for performance fees, session rates or private tuition income, which is where the entire livelihood sits. This is the sharpest case in the dataset of the schema's salary format failing a profession, and it recurs across most of Sector 10.

The Akashvani grading system is the closest thing to a professional standard and it is voluntary - it opens broadcast bookings and bars nothing. || [years_to_qualify] Six is a conservative reading and applies to the point of earning, not competence. Indian classical training routinely runs ten to fifteen years from a start in childhood, unpaid throughout, which makes it the longest and least-visible runway in this dataset. || [economics] The employed range describes salaried orchestra, ensemble and institutional posts, of which India has very few. It is close to fiction for most of this profession, where income is per performance, per session and per student. That is why the admin_review is required rather than optional.

one_liner: Writes and builds the music itself - for film, advertising, artists and their own releases.

Generative audio already produces usable library music, advertising beds and background loops, which is exactly what Jingle Composer, Music Programmer and much Arranger work is. Film Music Composer and Background Score Composer are protected by having to serve a director, a scene and a deadline through revisions - and Lyricist by writing in a specific Indian language for a specific voice.

one_liner: Performs and creates dance - classical, film, contemporary, folk and commercial.

one_liner: Reads a room and plays music live to it - clubs, weddings, festivals and events.
job_roles: Club DJ | Wedding & Event DJ | Radio DJ | Turntablist | Electronic Music Producer | Festival Performer | Mobile Disco Operator | Sound & Music Curator (Hospitality)

one_liner: Collects, sorts and disposes of what cities throw away, and keeps the sewers running.

one_liner: Grows crops on land they own, rent or work - the occupation most Indians still live from.
