nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and rising for a specific reason: Indian farm labour is becoming scarcer and costlier as rural workers move to construction and services, which is pushing mechanisation on holdings that were previously too small to justify it. Custom hiring is how that reaches a two-hectare farm. || [job_roles] Farm Equipment Service Technician is deliberately inside this profession rather than left out as too junior. It is entered through an ITI, needs no degree, exists in every taluka, and is one of the few technical livelihoods genuinely available to a student who stays in a small town.

one_liner: Turns crops into food that keeps, is safe to eat, and tastes the same every time.
job_roles: Food Technologist | Food Safety & Quality Manager | Product Development Technologist | Food Processing Supervisor | FSSAI Compliance Officer | Sensory Analyst | Dairy Technologist | Packaging Technologist (Food) | Food Microbiologist
entrance_exams: JEE Main | CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions
self_emp_route: Independent food safety consultancy and FSSAI licensing support for small manufacturers and restaurants, or a small processing unit. The consultancy route is real and growing because compliance obligations now reach very small businesses.
ai_reason: Low exposure, protected by physical product and by regulation. Food has to be made, tested and tasted, and somebody must sign the safety records. Sensory Analyst is the most exposed role on paper - preference modelling from panel data is statistics - but it is protected by needing human panels in the first place. Food Safety & Quality Manager is protected by carrying named responsibility under food law.
role_spread: [Food Safety & Quality Manager, FSSAI Compliance Officer] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Product Development Technologist, Sensory Analyst] higher: openness, naturalistic, reasoning / lower: conscientiousness || [Food Processing Supervisor] higher: bodily, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Mathematics. -> entrance_exam: CUET, a state agricultural university process, or JEE Main for the B.Tech Food Technology route. -> degree: B.Tech or B.Sc in Food Technology, Food Science or Dairy Technology. -> work: A food or dairy processing company, a quality and testing laboratory, a retail or restaurant chain's food safety team, or FSSAI-linked compliance work.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] Physics and Chemistry only, because listing Biology as well would wrongly shut out PCM students - Food Technology and B.Tech Food Engineering accept Mathematics in place of Biology at most universities. Over-restricting a subject gate is not a safe error in this dataset; it deletes a route a student actually has. || [demand_signal] High, and among the more reliable demand signals in this dataset. It rests on two things that are both still expanding: India's shift from unpackaged to packaged food, and the extension of FSSAI licensing and hygiene obligations down to very small businesses. Both create work that did not exist a decade ago. || [professional_sector] Promised here from Sector 3 rather than kept with the sciences. The method is applied chemistry and microbiology, but the object of concern is food - getting it from a field into a person safely - which is this sector.

one_liner: Keeps animals productive and healthy - milk, poultry, goats, and the systems around them.
job_roles: Dairy Farmer | Dairy Worker | Poultry Farm Supervisor | Livestock Extension Worker | Artificial Insemination Technician | Milk Procurement Officer | Animal Nutrition Specialist | Goat & Small Ruminant Farmer | Para-Veterinary Worker
self_emp_route: Owning animals is the profession for most people in it. A dairy herd of ten crossbred cows supplying a cooperative is a different economic proposition from working on someone else's farm, and it is the standard aspiration.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Animals are handled, fed, milked and treated by people, in sheds, twice a day, every day. Milk Procurement Officer carries the only real exposure through automated testing and digital payment systems at collection centres, which has already changed that role substantially without removing it.
role_spread: [Artificial Insemination Technician, Para-Veterinary Worker] higher: bodily, conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Milk Procurement Officer] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Poultry Farm Supervisor] higher: logical, attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for the farm and technician routes; PCB for a B.Sc or B.V.Sc route. -> training: A dairy or livestock diploma, an artificial insemination or para-vet certification, or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra course. Many enter with family experience and no certificate. -> work: Own herd, a dairy cooperative, a private dairy, a commercial poultry or feed company, or the state animal husbandry department. -> scale: Grow the herd, or move into procurement, extension or feed - the routes that convert animal work into a salary.
review_reason: No sourced figure for what a small dairy herd actually earns net of feed, which is the calculation every entrant to this profession is really making, and none for artificial insemination or para-vet technician incomes. The livestock share of household income is sourced; the unit economics of the herd are not.
nuances: [economics] Livestock contributed Rs 1,582 of an agricultural household's Rs 10,218 monthly income in 2018-19 - about 15 percent - and it is the most reliable component because milk sells daily while a crop sells twice a year. That daily cashflow, not the annual total, is why dairy matters to a small farming household. || [demand_signal] High, and India is the world's largest milk producer, but demand here means demand for OUTPUT rather than for salaried posts. Most of this profession is self-employment on a small herd; the salaried roles are in cooperatives, private dairies and feed companies and are far fewer.

one_liner: Grows fruit, vegetables, flowers, tea and spices - the high-value, high-risk end of farming.
job_roles: Horticulturist | Orchard Manager | Floriculture Specialist | Plantation Supervisor | Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager | Nursery Manager | Post-Harvest & Cold Chain Specialist | Landscape & Garden Supervisor | Mushroom & Speciality Crop Grower
self_emp_route: Growing high-value crops on own or leased land and selling direct - to an exporter, a retail chain, or through a Farmer Producer Organisation. Horticulture is where direct marketing actually changes the economics, because the produce is worth enough to justify the effort.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Growing, pruning, harvesting and grading are physical work on living plants in a field or a polyhouse. Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager carries a little exposure through automated climate and irrigation control, which is a tool the manager uses rather than a substitute for them.
role_spread: [Plantation Supervisor] higher: extraversion, conscientiousness, bodily / lower: openness || [Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager] higher: logical, attention_span, reasoning / lower: bodily || [Landscape & Garden Supervisor] higher: spatial, openness, extraversion / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream for the practical routes; PCB for a B.Sc Horticulture. -> training: B.Sc Horticulture, a diploma, or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra course. Many growers have none of these. -> work: Own orchard or polyhouse, a plantation company, a nursery, an export packhouse, or a landscaping firm. -> market: Secure a buyer before you plant. In horticulture the market, not the crop, is what fails.
review_reason: No sourced figures for horticulture returns per acre or for plantation sector wages, and the second matters: tea and coffee estate wages are set by state plantation labour rules and are published, which makes them fetchable and would anchor this record the way the NSS survey anchors Farmer.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate, and the risk profile is the opposite of staple farming. Horticulture returns several times more per hectare and has no minimum support price, no procurement and very little storage - so a price crash or a delayed truck destroys a season. Higher ceiling, no floor. || [economics] The range understates the upside and hides the variance. A polyhouse of capsicum or a well-marketed orchard can earn many times the figures shown; a season with no buyer earns nothing and the input cost is already spent.

one_liner: Catches or farms fish and shrimp - marine, inland and pond, and the cold chain behind it.
job_roles: Fisherman | Aquaculture Farm Manager | Shrimp Farm Technician | Fisheries Officer | Hatchery Technician | Fish Processing Supervisor | Aquatic Health Specialist | Ornamental Fish Breeder | Fish Seed Producer
entrance_exams: CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions | State fisheries department recruitment
self_emp_route: Owning ponds, a hatchery or a boat. Aquaculture is one of the higher-return self-employment routes in Indian agriculture and also one of the riskiest - a shrimp crop can fail completely.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Fishing, pond management and hatchery work are physical, outdoor and biological. Aquatic Health Specialist and Aquaculture Farm Manager use sensing and water quality monitoring that is increasingly automated, which improves the work rather than replacing the person standing at the pond edge deciding whether to harvest early.
role_spread: [Fisherman] higher: bodily, naturalistic, neuroticism / lower: logical || [Shrimp Farm Technician, Aquaculture Farm Manager] higher: logical, attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: neuroticism || [Fisheries Officer] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, logical / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for capture fishing and farm work; PCB for a B.F.Sc. -> training: B.F.Sc (4 years) for the professional and government routes; on-the-job or a short course for pond and hatchery work. -> work: Own or crew a boat, an aquaculture farm, a hatchery, a processing and export unit, or a state fisheries department. -> scale: Own ponds or a hatchery. In aquaculture the returns and the risk both sit with whoever owns the water.
review_reason: No sourced income figures for Indian capture fishing or for aquaculture returns per hectare, and the two are entirely different economies wrongly sharing one record's numbers. Fishermen's earnings in particular are shaped by boat-owner debt arrangements that no salary range can express.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and export-linked, which is the risk. Indian shrimp aquaculture is built on a small number of export markets and their sanitary and anti-dumping decisions; a single trade action can collapse prices for a season. Inland fish for the domestic market is far steadier and far less profitable. || [job_roles] Fisherman is included as the base layer and should be read with its role_spread entry. Marine capture fishing is among the most dangerous occupations in the country, is largely informal, and is frequently financed by debt to a boat owner - a structure that determines the income more than the catch does.

one_liner: Connects farmers to knowledge, inputs, credit and buyers - the business side of farming.
job_roles: Agricultural Extension Officer | Agri-Input Dealer | Farmer Producer Organisation Manager | Agri-Business Executive | Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer | Commodity & Mandi Trader | Agritech Field Executive | Warehouse & Procurement Officer | Krishi Vigyan Kendra Subject Specialist
entrance_exams: State agriculture department recruitment | IBPS PO | CAT | CUET (ICAR-UG) | Agri-business management entrances (IIM Ahmedabad PGP-FABM, IRMA)
self_emp_route: An agri-input dealership, a procurement or trading business, or independent advisory to FPOs and agritech firms. The dealership is the classic route and it is a retail business with a credit book attached.
ai_reason: Moderately exposed, and the exposure lands on the sector's most valuable function. Extension advice - which variety, when to sow, what this leaf spot is - is exactly what farmer advisory apps and image diagnosis now do at zero marginal cost, and Agritech Field Executive and much of Agricultural Extension Officer work is directly substitutable. What survives is where money and trust change hands: Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer, Agri-Input Dealer and Farmer Producer Organisation Manager all depend on knowing a specific farmer well enough to lend to them or sell for them.
role_spread: [Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer] higher: logical, conscientiousness, reasoning / lower: naturalistic || [Agri-Input Dealer] higher: extraversion, confidence, verbal / lower: openness || [Farmer Producer Organisation Manager] higher: agreeableness, verbal, conscientiousness / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream for the business roles; PCB or agriculture for extension posts. -> degree: B.Sc Agriculture for extension and technical roles; any degree, or an agri-business MBA, for the commercial ones. -> work: State agriculture department, a Krishi Vigyan Kendra, an input or seed company, a bank's agriculture desk, an agritech firm, or an FPO. -> independence: An input dealership or a procurement and trading business - the two commonest ways people in this profession end up working for themselves.
nuances: [entry_competition] Null. IBPS PO is named in entrance_exams because banks recruit Agriculture Field Officers and it is a genuine well-paid route - but making it the primary_gate would say the way to become an agri-business professional is to pass a banking examination, which is false for almost everyone in this profession. || [demand_signal] High, and it is the part of this sector where salaried jobs actually are. Agriculture employs about 45 percent of Indian workers but almost none of them are employees; the agri-input, agri-finance, agritech and FPO layer is where a graduate finds a salary in this sector. || [job_roles] Agri-Input Dealer is listed with its conflict of interest stated in the role_spread rather than hidden. In most of rural India the person selling the pesticide is also the person advising on whether it is needed, and a student entering this profession should understand that they are entering that position.

one_liner: Cooks for a living at scale - hotels, restaurants, canteens, cloud kitchens, ships.
job_roles: Commis Chef | Chef de Partie | Cook | Baker | Pastry Chef | Butcher | Cloud Kitchen Cook | Institutional & Canteen Cook | Private & Domestic Cook | Ship's Cook
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: Own restaurant, cloud kitchen, catering business or tiffin service. Catering and cloud kitchens need far less capital than a restaurant and are the realistic first step; this is also where almost all the money in the profession is.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Cooking is heat, hands, timing and taste in a physical kitchen, and no part of it is a text or image problem. Recipe generation touches menu development, which is a small slice of one senior role. The real technological pressure on this profession is different and worth naming: cloud kitchens and central production units are deskilling the line, turning cooks into assemblers of components made elsewhere.
role_spread: [Pastry Chef, Baker] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness, logical / lower: extraversion || [Institutional & Canteen Cook, Private & Domestic Cook] higher: conscientiousness, agreeableness / lower: openness, confidence || [Cloud Kitchen Cook] higher: bodily, short_term_memory, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none. Craft courses take class 10 pass; the B.Sc route needs class 12. -> training: An IHM craft course or diploma, a B.Sc Hospitality and Hotel Administration, or a kitchen apprenticeship with no certificate at all - all three are normal. -> work: Commis in a hotel or restaurant kitchen. Entry pay is low and hours are long; this is the profession's known filter. -> specialisation: A section - garde manger, butchery, bakery, Indian, continental. Specialising is what moves a cook off the entry wage.
nuances: [economics] The wide mid-career range is a real spread, not uncertainty. A hotel kitchen in a metro, a cruise line contract and a small-town restaurant pay very differently for the same skill, and the overseas route - cruise ships, the Gulf, hotel chains abroad - is why pathway is 'any' and is how many Indian chefs actually raise their income. || [demand_signal] High and among the most geographically distributed in this dataset. Every town has kitchens. That makes it one of very few skilled livelihoods genuinely available to a student who does not move to a city. || [entry_competition] Null, and it was wrong on the first pass. NCHMCT JEE was named as primary because it is the only quantified door in this sector - but this record's own entrance_exams note says most working Indian chefs never sat it, and both statements could not be true. Cooking is entered through a kitchen. The gate stays on Hotel & Restaurant Manager, where the IHM degree really is the main route.

one_liner: Serves guests food and drink and runs the room - restaurants, bars, banquets, trains, air.
job_roles: Steward | Waiter | Restaurant Captain | Bartender | Barista | Sommelier | Banquet Service Staff | Room Service Attendant | Cafe & QSR Service Crew
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: A cafe, bar or small restaurant of your own, or a catering and bartending service for events. Bartending in particular is a genuine freelance market at weddings and parties.
ai_reason: Low AI exposure and high exposure to something else. Ordering has already moved to apps and QR menus, and Cafe & QSR Service Crew and Room Service Attendant are the roles that shrinks - but that is self-service automation, not AI. What holds is hospitality itself: reading a table, fixing a complaint, and making a guest feel looked after. Sommelier and Bartender are protected further by knowledge and personality being the product.
role_spread: [Bartender, Sommelier] higher: long_term_memory, extraversion, openness / lower: conscientiousness || [Banquet Service Staff, Cafe & QSR Service Crew] higher: bodily, conscientiousness / lower: verbal, openness || [Restaurant Captain] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, confidence / lower: neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for most service roles; class 12 for hotel management programmes. -> training: An IHM or private hospitality course, a THSC-aligned certification, or straight on-the-job training. Most enter with the last. -> work: Restaurant, hotel, cafe chain, catering company, railway or airline catering, or a cruise line. -> specialisation: Bar, wine, or supervision. Beverage specialisation is the clearest way to raise earnings inside service.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian hospitality service staff, and the record cannot show tips, service charge or the overseas premium - which between them are much of the real income. Cruise line and Gulf contract pay in particular is the difference between this being a low-wage job and a genuine earner, and no figure for it was found.
nuances: [economics] Fails nothing on the filter but sits low, and the record should be read with tips and service charge in mind - neither is captured here and both are material in hotels and premium restaurants. The overseas route, especially cruise lines and the Gulf, is again where earnings change. || [demand_signal] High and permanently entry-friendly. This profession, along with retail in Sector 5, is one of the main places an Indian school-leaver with no qualification actually finds formal-sector work.

one_liner: Keeps rooms, buildings and linen clean and ready - hotels, hospitals, offices, homestays.
job_roles: Housekeeping Attendant | Room Attendant | Housekeeping Supervisor | Laundry Supervisor | Linen & Uniform Room Attendant | Public Area Attendant | Facility Housekeeping Executive | Hospital Housekeeping Attendant | Homestay & Guesthouse Caretaker
self_emp_route: A small housekeeping or facility services contract - a team, supplies and a client. It is a low-capital services business and it is how supervisors in this trade raise their income.
ai_reason: Effectively unexposed to AI, and this is another case where naming AI is the wrong risk. Cleaning a room is physical work in an unstructured space. The technology that matters is mechanised cleaning equipment, which raises output per worker rather than replacing the worker, and scheduling software, which has already changed how contract housekeeping is managed.
role_spread: [Hospital Housekeeping Attendant] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: extraversion, openness || [Housekeeping Supervisor, Facility Housekeeping Executive] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, logical / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Class 8 or 10 is typical. -> training: On-the-job, or a short THSC-aligned housekeeping certification. Hospital housekeeping requires infection-control training. -> work: Hotel, hospital, facility management contractor, corporate office or serviced apartment. Most of it is contract employment through an agency rather than direct. -> progression: Supervisor, then executive. Or run a homestay or a small housekeeping contract of your own.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian housekeeping staff, and the more important missing distinction is between direct hotel employment and agency contract employment, which is where pay, provident fund and security actually differ. No figure either for what a small housekeeping contract earns, which is the named route up.
nuances: [economics] Fails the compensation filter, and it is one of the largest formal-sector entry occupations available to Indian women without qualifications. Almost all of it is CONTRACT employment through a facility management agency rather than direct employment by the hotel or hospital, which determines pay, benefits and job security more than the employer's name does. || [demand_signal] High and growing with organised retail, hospitals, offices and hotels. It is also one of the few occupations in this dataset where formalisation is genuinely increasing - facility management contracting has moved a large amount of this work from informal to at least nominally formal employment.

one_liner: Runs the place - rooms, covers, staff, cost, and what happens when a guest is unhappy.
job_roles: Front Office Executive | Guest Relations Executive | Duty Manager | Restaurant Manager | Food & Beverage Manager | Revenue & Reservations Executive | Banquet & Events Manager | Resort Operations Executive | Hostel & Homestay Manager
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: Own restaurant, homestay, boutique hotel or cloud kitchen brand. Very common in this profession, and the operational knowledge transfers directly - which is why hospitality graduates start businesses at a higher rate than most.
ai_reason: Moderately exposed on the desk and protected on the floor. Revenue & Reservations Executive is the most exposed role - dynamic pricing is already algorithmic and improving - and routine reservations and enquiry handling have largely moved to booking platforms and chat. Duty Manager, Front Office Executive and Restaurant Manager are protected by being the person physically accountable when something goes wrong at eleven at night.
role_spread: [Revenue & Reservations Executive] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: bodily || [Front Office Executive, Guest Relations Executive] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, confidence / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> entrance_exam: NCHMCT JEE for the Institutes of Hotel Management, or a state or private institute admission. -> degree: B.Sc Hospitality and Hotel Administration (3 years), or any degree plus hotel experience. -> work: Management trainee or front office executive, then a section. Progression is by rotating through departments.
nuances: [entry_competition] Null. NCHMCT JEE was recorded here on the first pass and removed on review: this record is mid_stream_entry 'after_any_degree', its own path_to_entry says 'any degree plus hotel experience', and the exam offers over 12,000 seats. A gate that admits any graduate and is not scarce is not the thing that determines who reaches the profession. || [economics] The employed range is Indian. The profession's real economics for many people are overseas - Gulf hotels, cruise lines and international chains - and that pathway is a large part of why students choose hotel management. It is why pathway is 'any' and it is not visible in these numbers. || [demand_signal] High, and unusually resilient in a specific way: hospitality collapsed completely during the pandemic and rebuilt, and the sector's hiring now runs ahead of the supply of trained people because a cohort left the industry and did not return.

one_liner: Plans, sells and guides travel - itineraries, tickets, tours and the people on them.
job_roles: Travel Consultant | Tour Operator | Tour Guide | Destination Specialist | Ticketing & Reservations Executive | Travel Sales Executive | Tour Manager | Pilgrimage & Cultural Tour Coordinator | Corporate Travel Coordinator
entrance_exams: Ministry of Tourism regional guide training and licensing | IATA and travel agency certifications
self_emp_route: An independent tour operation, a niche travel business - wildlife, pilgrimage, adventure, weddings abroad - or freelance guiding. Low capital and high dependence on repeat customers and reviews.
ai_reason: The most AI-exposed profession in this sector, and the damage arrived before AI did. Ticketing & Reservations Executive and Travel Consultant lost their market to online booking over two decades, and language models finish the job on itinerary planning and destination advice - both are high-retrievable-knowledge tasks. What survives is physical presence and accountability: Tour Guide, licensed and standing in front of the monument, and Tour Manager, responsible for thirty people in a foreign country when something goes wrong.

one_liner: Makes an event happen - weddings, conferences, concerts, exhibitions, sport.

one_liner: Keeps an aircraft cabin safe and its passengers looked after - a safety job that serves food.

one_liner: Navigates and commands a cargo ship - the deck side of the merchant marine.

entrance_exams: IMU CET | DG Shipping approved pre-sea training admissions | Company-sponsored cadet schemes
ai_reason: Very low exposure. Ships are increasingly automated and crewed by fewer people, but a certificated officer must be aboard and personally answerable for the safe navigation of the vessel under international convention. Autonomous shipping is real and slow, and the regulatory requirement for a licensed human on watch is what this profession rests on. Marine Surveyor Trainee and Port Operations Officer carry more exposure through documentation and inspection tooling.

path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics with 60 percent aggregate and 50 percent in English. Medical standard is absolute: 6/6 vision without aids and no colour blindness. -> entrance_exam: IMU CET or a DG Shipping approved institute's admission, plus a company sponsorship test. -> training: Either a one-year Diploma in Nautical Science or a three-year B.Sc Nautical Science, at a DG Shipping approved institute. Both lead to the same certificate and both cost like a degree - the DNS is a one-year course priced in lakhs. -> sea_time: 18 months of Structured Shipboard Training as a Deck Cadet. THIS REQUIRES A COMPANY SPONSORSHIP and is the real bottleneck. -> certification: Four months post-sea shore training, the STCW courses, and the Second Mates examination conducted by the Directorate General of Shipping. Passing awards the Second Mates (FG) Certificate of Competency.
review_reason: The highest figure and the widest spread anywhere in Sectors 8 to 18 - 13 to 32 lakh - and entirely unsourced. A fetchable anchor exists and should be used: the NUSI-MUI and INSA collective bargaining wage scales publish monthly rates for a Third Officer on Indian-flag foreign-going ships, and ITF minimum scales cover the international floor. Sourcing it would make this the sector's one statutory-style anchor, as the Majithia award is for Sector 9.
nuances: [licensing_body] Tier A. The Second Mates (Foreign Going) Certificate of Competency is issued by the Directorate General of Shipping after its own examination, and serving as a deck officer without one is unlawful. This is the same statutory structure as the MEO certificates recorded for Marine Engineer in Sector 2. || [path_to_entry] The binding constraint is not academic. Eighteen months of shipboard training requires a shipping company to sponsor a cadet berth, and the number of berths is far smaller than the number of people completing pre-sea courses. Students routinely pay for a diploma and then cannot proceed. Any institute that does not guarantee sponsorship in writing should be treated with suspicion. || [economics] The cost of entry is the part students underestimate. A DG Shipping approved pre-sea course is priced in lakhs whether it is the one-year diploma or the three-year degree, it is paid up front, and it does not guarantee the cadet berth that the certificate depends on. Money spent before sponsorship is money at risk. || [class12_prerequisite] PCM is required and so is a MEDICAL standard that no other profession in this dataset imposes: uncorrected 6/6 vision and no colour blindness. That excludes a large number of academically eligible students, and it should be checked before any money is spent. || [economics] Set level with Marine Engineer in Sector 2 rather than above it. Deck and engine officers hold parallel Certificates of Competency on the same ship under the same international convention, and a gap between them was not defensible. The highest earnings in this sector by a wide margin, and they are earned at sea in tax-advantaged foreign-going service, away from home for months. Shore roles after sailing pay substantially less, which is the trade every officer eventually makes.

one_liner: Finds and reads the physical remains of the past - excavation, survey, dating, publication.

entrance_exams: CUET UG | CUET PG | UGC NET | Institute of Archaeology (ASI) PGDA admission
self_emp_route: Heritage impact assessment and archaeological consultancy for infrastructure projects, which is a real and growing market because large projects must assess archaeological impact. It requires the field credibility that only excavation experience gives.
ai_reason: Low exposure and protected by the ground. Evidence has to be excavated, recorded and physically handled, and stratigraphy is read in a trench by a person who is standing in it. Archaeological Draughtsman is the most exposed role, since site drawing and plan production have largely moved to photogrammetry and digital modelling. Epigraphist carries genuine exposure too - machine reading of inscriptions and scripts is improving - but the interpretation of a damaged, ambiguous text remains judgment.

path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Arts is the usual route and science backgrounds are valued for the analytical specialisms. -> degree: BA in History, Archaeology or Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology. -> masters: MA in Archaeology, or the two-year Post Graduate Diploma at the Institute of Archaeology, ASI - which is the recognised professional route and admits very few. -> field_training: Excavation seasons. nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and the distinction matters. The AMASR Act 1958 regulates EXCAVATION - digging is not open to anyone who wants to - but that is a permit regime over an activity, not a register of practitioners. No council licenses archaeologists and nobody is struck off, and survey, documentation, museum and teaching work needs no authorisation at all. Hence Tier B rather than Tier A. || [demand_signal] Low, and honestly so. ASI and state archaeology posts are few and filled irregularly, university positions depend on UGC NET and a doctorate, and the field is romanticised far beyond its employment. The growing part is heritage impact assessment for infrastructure, which is consultancy rather than research. || [years_to_qualify] Seven years, and for most people it is more - a permanent post generally needs a doctorate on top. one_liner: Looks after collections and makes them usable - cataloguing, storage, display, access.

entrance_exams: CUET UG | CUET PG | UGC NET
self_emp_route: Freelance cataloguing, collection documentation and exhibition research for private collectors, galleries and corporate collections. A thin market and it depends on the digital skills more than the curatorial ones.
ai_reason: Genuinely contested and the profession is splitting. Cataloguing, metadata generation and condition-report drafting are directly automatable, and Gallery Assistant and much Collections Manager work is routine documentation. What has grown rather than shrunk is Digital Collections Officer - when description became cheap, deciding what to digitise and how to structure access became the job - and Museum Education Officer, which is teaching in a room.

path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: BA in History, Art History, Archaeology or a related discipline. -> specialisation: MA in Museology, Archival Studies or Art History, or a Library and Information Science qualification for the records side. -> work: National or state museum, the National Archives, a university collection, a private or corporate museum, or a records department.

India has an enormous quantity of material and very few funded posts to look after it; state museums are chronically understaffed and many positions go unfilled rather than being advertised. The growth is in private and corporate collections and in digitisation projects. || [professional_sector] Distinguished from Librarian & Information Professional in Sector 12 by purpose. A librarian exists so a community can LEARN, which is education; an archivist exists so material SURVIVES and remains accessible, which is heritage. The records management roles sit awkwardly across that line.

one_liner: Stops old things falling apart - paintings, manuscripts, sculpture, textiles, buildings.
job_roles: Art Conservator | Paintings Conservator | Manuscript & Paper Conservator | Textile Conservator | Stone & Sculpture Conservator | Architectural Conservator | Preventive Conservation Officer | Conservation Scientist | Conservation Technician
entrance_exams: CUET PG | National Museum Institute admission
self_emp_route: Private conservation practice - treating works for collectors, galleries, temples and trusts, or architectural conservation consultancy. Independent practice is normal in this profession because institutional posts are so few.
ai_reason: Among the least exposed professions in this sector and in the dataset. Conservation is hands on an irreplaceable physical object where a mistake cannot be undone, and every treatment decision is a judgment about a unique thing. Conservation Scientist carries some exposure through automated analysis of spectra and imaging, which is a tool the conservator uses. Nothing in the generative wave touches the bench.

path_to_entry: class_11_12: Science is a real advantage - conservation is applied chemistry as much as craft - but arts backgrounds are accepted. -> degree: BSc or BA, then an MA or MSc in Conservation or Art Conservation. The National Museum Institute is the main Indian route and takes very few students. -> apprenticeship: Supervised bench practice. Conservation is a craft with an irreversible failure mode and it is learned under someone. -> work: National or state museum, ASI, INTACH, a private conservation studio, or an architectural conservation practice.

Architectural conservation in particular is project-fee work at a completely different scale from object conservation, and one range covers both.
nuances: [profession] Promised here from Sector 8 and it belongs here. The skill is close to fine art and craft, but the object of concern is HERITAGE and its survival, not making something new. The conservator's whole discipline is subordinating their own hand to what the original maker did. || [demand_signal] Low in posts and enormous in need, which is the sector's recurring shape. India holds a vast quantity of deteriorating material and trains a handful of conservators a year. Scarcity here has not produced high pay, because the people who own the material mostly cannot fund the work.

one_liner: Conducts worship, rites and religious teaching - temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras.

ai_reason: Very low exposure, and for a reason no other profession in this dataset has. What is purchased here is the presence of a person the family and the tradition accept as authorised to perform the rite. That authority is social and religious, and it cannot be supplied by a machine at any capability level. Astrologer & Ritual Consultant is the only role with real exposure, because chart generation and standard readings are already software - but there too the client is paying for a person.
role_spread: [Temple Administrator] higher: conscientiousness, logical, extraversion / lower: bodily || [Purohit & Ritual Specialist, Astrologer & Ritual Consultant] higher: verbal, extraversion, long_term_memory / lower: agreeableness || [Religious Teacher] higher: verbal, long_term_memory, agreeableness / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Training in most traditions begins in childhood and runs in parallel with or instead of school. -> training: Traditional study - a pathshala, madrasa, seminary, gurukul or seminary equivalent - lasting years, and in several traditions requiring memorisation of a large corpus. -> recognition: Recognition by the tradition and by a community. There is no examination and no certificate anyone outside the tradition checks. -> work: An institution's post, or independent practice serving families in a locality. In several states temple appointments are made by a government religious endowments department.

One thing IS fetchable and would materially improve the record: several state governments run religious endowments departments that appoint and pay temple staff on published scales, which would anchor at least the formal half. A priest at a major temple, a salaried imam, and a purohit doing weekend ceremonies in a small town are three different economies sharing one record. Placing it here rather than nowhere is a decision that the object of concern is culture and belief, not that any claim is being made about the beliefs themselves. || [years_to_qualify] Six years is a rough figure for reaching independent practice, and it understates several traditions badly - memorising the Quran, or Vedic recitation to ritual standard, takes far longer and usually begins in childhood.

one_liner: Paints faces for cameras, weddings and stages - and makes them survive lights and hours.
job_roles: Makeup Artist | Makeup & Hair Artist | Bridal Makeup Artist | Film & Television Makeup Artist | Fashion & Editorial Makeup Artist | Special Effects Makeup Artist | Prosthetics & Character Makeup Artist | Airbrush Makeup Specialist | Makeup Retail Consultant | Makeup Educator
self_emp_route: Freelance bridal, film and fashion work booked directly or through agencies. This profession is essentially entirely self-employed, and bridal season is where the income is concentrated.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Makeup is applied by hand to a specific face and must survive hours and lights. Digital retouching has been available for two decades and did not remove the job, because the photograph is not the only deliverable - the person has to walk around looking like that. Makeup Retail Consultant carries the exposure, through virtual try-on tools that have already changed beauty retail.
role_spread: [Special Effects Makeup Artist, Prosthetics & Character Makeup Artist] higher: spatial, openness, bodily / lower: extraversion || [Makeup Retail Consultant] higher: extraversion, verbal, agreeableness / lower: attention_span || [Bridal Makeup Artist] higher: conscientiousness, emotional_intelligence, bodily / lower: neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> training: A professional makeup course, or assisting an established artist. Assisting is how the film and fashion side is genuinely entered. -> portfolio: Photographed work. This profession hires entirely on images, which is why building a portfolio through unpaid shoots is standard. -> work: Bridal clients, a salon, film and television production, fashion shoots, or beauty retail.
nuances: [profession] Routed here from Sector 8 rather than kept with design. The skill is close to painting and the employers are film and fashion, but the object of concern is a treatment applied to a living person's body - which is what this sector is - and the constraints that govern it are skin, hygiene and hours worn, not composition. || [economics] Concentrated and seasonal. Bridal work in the Indian wedding season is where most of the money is, and a well-known bridal artist earns multiples of the range shown. Film and television work pays per day and is metro-based. Neither is visible in an annual employed figure.

one_liner: Gives therapeutic and relaxation treatments - spas, hotels, wellness centres, homes.
job_roles: Spa Therapist | Massage Therapist | Reflexologist | Aromatherapist | Hydrotherapy & Body Treatment Therapist | Spa Receptionist & Coordinator | Wellness Centre Supervisor | Visually Impaired Massage Therapist | Panchakarma Therapist | Ayurveda Therapist | Abhyanga & Oil Therapy Technician | Wellness Retreat Therapist
entrance_exams: Private spa and massage academy certifications
self_emp_route: Home-visit practice and independent clients, which is common and better paid than salon employment. Hotel and cruise ship contracts are the other route and pay considerably more.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Manual therapy is hands on a body reading tension and responding to it, and no part of that is digital. Massage devices and chairs exist and have existed for decades without displacing therapists, because the judgment about pressure and contraindication is the service. Spa Receptionist & Coordinator carries the only real exposure through booking automation.
role_spread: [Visually Impaired Massage Therapist] higher: bodily, attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: spatial || [Panchakarma Therapist, Ayurveda Therapist, Wellness Retreat Therapist] higher: naturalistic, conscientiousness, long_term_memory / lower: extraversion || [Wellness Centre Supervisor, Spa Receptionist & Coordinator] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, extraversion / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Class 10 is typical. -> training: A spa therapy or massage course - BWSSC/NSQF aligned, a hotel spa academy, or a specialist programme. Anatomy and contraindications are the parts that matter. -> work: Hotel spa, standalone spa or wellness centre, cruise ship, or home service. -> specialisation: A modality, or supervision. The physical toll of full-time treatment work is real and most therapists plan around it.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian spa or massage therapists, and none for cruise or overseas contract rates, which are the best-paid route. A second gap that is not about money: the working conditions and safety of practitioners in the informal home-service segment are a real concern and nothing in this record can express them.
nuances: [job_roles] AYURVEDA & PANCHAKARMA THERAPIST WAS BUILT AS A SEPARATE PROFESSION AND MERGED IN ON REVIEW, on the Solar Panel Technician precedent in DECISIONS.md 8.95 - same object of concern, same skill set plus a specialisation. The evidence was that the two records came out numerically identical on every economic field: cost 1.0, early 1.5-3.6, mid 2.7-7.0, midpoint 4.85, payback 0.39, certificate tier, two years, open entry. Two professions a builder cannot tell apart will always surface together in a psychometric recommender, which is the noise the merge test exists to prevent. || [path_to_entry] One distinction survives the merge and must not be lost: a panchakarma THERAPIST is not an Ayurveda DOCTOR. Ayurveda Doctor in Sector 4 is a five-and-a-half-year BAMS with statutory registration and the right to diagnose and prescribe; the therapist performs treatments under that prescription. Marketing routinely conflates the two, which is how unqualified people come to present as Ayurvedic physicians. || [licensing_body] Null, and this profession needs the point made more sharply than most. Nothing in India registers a massage therapist or sets a standard for training in anatomy and contraindications, and the absence of regulation also leaves practitioners - who are disproportionately women and migrants working in private rooms - without a professional standing that would protect them. It is a safety gap in both directions. || [demand_signal] Moderate and split by segment. Hotel and wellness-tourism spa work is growing and pays reasonably; the standalone and home-service market is crowded and informal. Cruise ship and overseas contracts are the highest-paying route and are why pathway is 'any'.

one_liner: Makes permanent marks on people - tattooing, piercing, and the hygiene that must go with it.
job_roles: Tattoo Artist | Body Piercer | Permanent Makeup Artist | Tattoo Removal Technician | Scalp Micropigmentation Technician | Studio Hygiene & Sterilisation Technician | Tattoo Design Artist
self_emp_route: Own studio or a rented chair. This is the normal form of the profession and the artist's own following is the entire business.
ai_reason: Low exposure with one real crack. Tattoo Design Artist is directly exposed - generating tattoo designs is exactly what image models do, and clients now arrive with generated references. But the application is manual work on living skin with an irreversible result, and Tattoo Artist, Body Piercer and Permanent Makeup Artist are protected by that completely. What has changed is that the drawing is worth less and the hand is worth more.
role_spread: [Studio Hygiene & Sterilisation Technician] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Tattoo Design Artist] higher: openness, spatial, verbal / lower: bodily || [Permanent Makeup Artist, Scalp Micropigmentation Technician] higher: attention_span, spatial, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Drawing ability matters and is not certified. -> training: Apprenticeship in a studio. There is no recognised Indian qualification, and courses sold as certification are not a substitute for supervised practice on skin. -> hygiene: Bloodborne pathogen and sterilisation training. This is the part that matters and nothing compels it. -> work: Studio artist, then your own studio or chair. Reputation is built on a public portfolio and healed work.
nuances: [profession] Routed here from Sector 8 and the decision is confirmed. The skill is drawing, which pointed at design - but the object of concern is a permanent, irreversible modification of a living person's body, governed by hygiene, consent and bloodborne infection risk. Those constraints belong to personal care, not to the design of objects. || [licensing_body] Null, and this is the most serious unregulated-practice gap in the sector. Tattooing and piercing break the skin and carry hepatitis and HIV transmission risk, and India has no national licensing, no mandatory sterilisation standard and no inspection regime for studios. A student entering this trade should understand that the hygiene discipline is entirely on them.
